1. Introduction

     The following is a well-known conjecture in graph theory by Caccetta and Häggkvist [5] from 1978.


Conjecture 1 ([5]). In an n-vertex digraph with minimum out-degree r, there exists a directed cycle of length at most ⌈ nr ⌉.


    The conjecture is still open. For a history of the studying of this problem, see, e.g., the references in [11--13].
    Given a graph G and an edge coloring (not necessarily proper) with m colors λ : E (G ) → [m], for each i ∈ [m] the edge
set λ−1 (i ) is called a color class, and a subgraph H of G is rainbow if no two edges of H belong to the same color class. The
rainbow girth of G is the minimum length of a rainbow cycle in G (∞ if there is no rainbow cycle). In [2], a generalization
of the Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture is raised by Aharoni.


Conjecture 2 ([2]). For an n-vertex graph G and an edge coloring of G with n colors, if each color class is of size at least r, then the
rainbow girth at most ⌈ nr ⌉.


    A more general version of the conjecture (see, e.g., [3, Conjecture 1.5]) states that for a family ( F 1 , . . . , F n ) of edge sets
on a vertex set of size n, where each F i has size r and the sets are not necessarily disjoint, there exists a cycle of length at
most ⌈ nr ⌉ in which each edge comes from a distinct set in the family. For our purposes, we may assume that the sets F i are
disjoint: otherwise, there exists a digon, i.e., a cycle of length 2, whose edges are from distinct sets.

the n-vertex graph on {x1 , . . . , xn } and each color class forms a star of size r with the form {xi xi +1 , . . . , xi xi +r } for 1 ≤ i ≤ n,

    Regarding Conjecture 2, DeVos et al. [7] proved that the conjecture is true when r = 2. For the case that each color class
is of size 1 or 2, a more explicit bound on the rainbow girth is given in [3].

Theorem 1 ([3]). For an n-vertex graph and an edge coloring with n colors, if p color classes are of size 1 and n − p color classes are of

size 2, then the rainbow girth is at most ⌈ 2 ⌉.


   The r = 3 case of Conjecture 2 is still open, while Clinch et al. [6] proved that for r = 3 the rainbow girth is at most 4n

7. For general r, Hompe and Spirkl [10] proved that there exists a constant 0 < C ≤ 1011 such that the rainbow girth is
at most C nr . Recently, Hompe and Huynh [9] proved a stronger result that the rainbow girth is at most nr + αr for some
positive constant αr depending on r.
   As the bound on the rainbow girth in Conjecture 2 is linear in n and in all the known extremal examples the color
classes are stars, another direction is to study when the rainbow girth is small, say, logarithmic in n.

Theorem 2 ([1]). There exists C > 0 such that for any n-vertex graph and edge coloring with n colors, if each color class contains a
matching of size 2, then the rainbow girth is at most C log n.

   In [8], the result is strengthened to the following.

Theorem 3 ([8]). For any α > 12 , there exists C > 0 such that the following holds. Let G be an n-vertex graph admitting an edge
coloring with n colors such that each color class is non-empty. If there are at least αn color classes, each of which contains a matching
of size 2, then the rainbow girth of G is at most C log n.

and having linear rainbow girth, shows that the condition           α>     2

   In this note, we further strengthen the above result.

Theorem 4. For any α , β ≥ 0 with 2α + β > 1, there exists C > 0 such that the following holds. Let G be an n-vertex graph admitting
an edge coloring with n colors. If the family of color classes ℱ = ( F 1 , . . . , F n ) satisfies the following conditions:

  • each color class is non-empty,
  • there exists ℱ M ⊆ ℱ such that |ℱ M | = αn and each color class in ℱ M contains a matching of size 2,
  • and there exists ℱ S ⊆ ℱ \ ℱ M such that |ℱ S | = β n and each color class in ℱ S contains a star of size 2.

Then the rainbow girth of G is at most C log n.

Remark 5. To have logarithmic rainbow girth, the condition 2α + β > 1 in Theorem 4 is tight. See Example 17.

   In Theorem 14, we prove a slightly stronger result, which allows the numbers of color classes to be less than those
in Theorem 4. As an immediate implication, if each of the n color classes is of size at least 2, then a small fraction of color
classes that contain a matching of size 2 guarantee the rainbow girth to be logarithmic.

Corollary 6. For any α > 0, there exists C > 0 such that the following holds. Let G be an n-vertex graph admitting an edge coloring
with n colors such that each color class is of size at least 2. If there are at least αn color classes, each of which contains a matching of
size 2, then the rainbow girth of G is at most C log n.

   Since a non-star edge set that does not contain a matching of size 2 is a triangle, it was shown in [3] that for an n-vertex
graph admitting an edge coloring with n colors, if each color class contains a triangle, then the rainbow girth is O (log n).
This result is extended in [8] by considering a mixed case.

Theorem 7 ([8]). There exists C > 0 such that for any n-vertex graph and edge coloring with n colors, if each color class contains either
a matching of size 2 or a triangle, then the rainbow girth is at most C log n.

    We further extend Corollary 6 and Theorem 7 and show that a small fraction of non-star color classes make the rainbow
girth logarithmic.

2.5. Tightness of the condition 2α + β > 1 in Theorem 4

    To get logarithmic rainbow girth in Theorem 4, it is necessary to assume that 2α + β > 1. For α , β ≥ 0 with 2α + β = 1,
the following is an example of an n-vertex graph satisfying all the other conditions in Theorem 4, whose rainbow girth is
linear in n.
